purpose: Initial historical extraction evidence, deliberately nonspatial until district footprints are verified. Never treat an artifact or smelter location as an ore coordinate.

records.region: Minong district, Isle Royale, Lake Superior, United States
records.period: Indigenous mining at least 4500 years ago; industrial mining in the nineteenth century
records.form: Native copper; primary bedrock mining. Regional glacial drift copper requires a separate transport footprint.
records.grade_note: NPS historical account describes stamp rock at about 1.5% Cu that was not profitable to stamp and transport at that operation. This is not a universal grade threshold.
records.confidence: Official archaeological/historical account; local footprint not digitized
records.review_required: Use public district extent; do not recover redacted archaeological coordinates.

records.period: Bronze Age and later, with distinct later mining phases
records.form: Early alluvial cassiterite; exposed copper lodes reported as probable early copper source
records.source_feature_id: BGS memoir sheets 351 and 358, Economic geology
records.confidence: Survey synthesis; not a dated claim for every mapped lode
records.review_required: Digitize source areas and drainage; keep probable copper source interpretation qualified.

records.region: Gonamena, Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, United Kingdom
records.form: Residual/eluvial cassiterite released by weathering and concentrated with water
records.review_required: Import licensed official extent if suitable; do not mark this particular streamwork Bronze Age.

records.period: Chalcolithic open-pit evidence at Merkavot 1 and later second-millennium BCE extraction
records.form: Copper nodules in valley conglomerate gravels; later shafts and underground extraction
records.source_feature_id: Central Timna Valley Project, Merkavot investigations
records.confidence: Excavator account with dating study; regional outline not digitized
records.review_required: Match geology-source footprint, not only a smelting site; keep distinct technological periods.

records.period: Mining evidence dated 1400–1640 CE; Smelterskop smelting generally seventeenth–nineteenth centuries
records.form: Evidence discussed for placer cassiterite formerly present, alongside regional primary tin
records.source_feature_id: 2025 mining archaeology study and Chirikure et al. 2010
records.review_required: Do not equate bronze use from 1200 CE with directly dated extraction; reconstruct exhausted placers separately from modern reserves.

records.period: Third millennium BCE, including about 2600 BCE
records.form: Cassiterite processing inferred from ore-dressing equipment, crucibles, slags and experiments
records.source_feature_id: Yener and Vandiver 1993; Earl and Özbal 1996
records.confidence: Excavation-based interpretation; quantitative production and provenance not established here
records.review_required: Review contested scale of production; do not assume this supplied every nearby bronze object.

records.period: Slag dated 1900–1400 BCE; ancient mining galleries described
records.form: Oxidized mixed Cu–Sn mineralization; slag comparison supports nearby ore use
records.confidence: Primary geological and archaeological studies; not a global trade attribution
records.review_required: Slag is approximately 4 km from the deposit: keep find point separate from ore source. No Uluburun provenance claim.
